extracted.intended_audience: Marine Corps and DoD contracting officers, A-76 program managers, acquisition professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for planning, staffing, executing, and managing OMB Circular A-76 competitive sourcing (commercial activity) studies across DoD installations, with emphasis on contracting officers and source selection processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with FAR and execution of acquisition strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting officers and A-76 teams must build an acquisition strategy in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and follow that plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to create and follow FAR-compliant processes (e.g., improper formation of the Source Selection Evaluation Board) can lead to protests, Comptroller General mandates to re-compete, and overturned decisions (DZS/Baker LLC and Morrison Knudsen example). Ensure creation, documentation, and strict adherence to the acquisition strategy from the outset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound management structure and senior leadership involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 studies require a sound management structure; involving senior installation management, including the installation commander, lends credibility and guidance to the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey responses recommended integrated bodies (e.g., an A-76 Council or Integrated Product Team). Where major commands participate, support ranges from identifying candidates to developing PWSs. Lack of command-level involvement typically leaves management to individual installations and may weaken the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-office-like management of A-76 studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the complexity of competitive sourcing studies, management should be similar to that used for major weapon systems — a 'quasi' program office for A-76 studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt program-management practices (dedicated program manager, formal oversight, lifecycle planning) to handle complexities, timelines, and risks rather than ad-hoc or purely part-time structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing: full-time program manager and team assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Installations should have a full-time program manager and examine assigning A-76 study team members on a full-time basis to meet schedules and program needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade-offs exist: full-time staff improve schedule adherence and focus but may lose touch with day-to-day operations. Mitigate loss of technical competence by having team members work closely with the activities under study when developing the PWS. Timelines are critical because savings are often programmed into future budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding conflicts of interest and evaluator integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff assignments to the A-76 team, SSEB, and SSAC must avoid conflicts of interest and legal violations; evaluators must be beyond reproach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile conflict-of-interest databases listing employees forbidden from participating; develop lists of 'desirable' and 'undesirable' personnel. Use military lawyers familiar with contracting statutes to scrub candidate lists. Failure to identify conflicts risks protests and restarting acquisitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition strategy importance and early contract-type selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The acquisition strategy is the single most important A-76 document and should be the team's focus from program onset; the contract type should be chosen early based on requirements, maturity of cost analysis, and acceptable risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not default to one contract type. Consider nature of work (variable costs like food services argue against FFP), maturity of cost data, and risk-sharing. Early selection prevents unnecessary changes later and frames solicitation/evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use and administration of incentive/award-fee contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed-Price-Incentive-Firm, Fixed-Price Award-Fee, and cost-reimbursement contracts may be appropriate depending on circumstances; award-fee contracts have specific administrative requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before using award-fee/incentive approaches, ensure: (1) administrative costs of evaluations do not exceed expected benefits; (2) procedures are established for award-fee evaluation; (3) periodic evaluations against an award-fee plan are provided (government unilateral judgment not subject to Disputes Clause); (4) award amounts are sufficient to motivate excellence in quality, timeliness, technical ingenuity, and cost-effective management. Account for admin costs and plan evaluation procedures in the acquisition strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and measurement of past performance (including Government/MEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Past performance is a key indicator for services contracts, but guidance is lacking on measuring Government (MEO) past performance; contracting officers must decide how to evaluate and normalize past performance data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require past-performance data from firms; for MEO (which lacks implemented past performance), consider measuring current Government organization's performance but recognize flaws. If evaluating past performance, set grading criteria and normalize scores for firms without such data; apply same method to MEO proposal. Do not dismiss past performance outright—it can be critical in selecting the firm to compete against the MEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best value decision-making rather than lowest-price-only
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular A-76 provides for best value comparisons, but practice often defaults to lowest-priced technically acceptable suppliers; studies should enable 'best value' decisions considering the totality of offers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To choose best value, A-76 implementation must allow awarding contracts on bases other than price (e.g., past performance, technical approach, management plans). Consider informing MEO of areas for reexamination if circumstances warrant so MEO can adjust to be competitive, while balancing fairness concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control communications to prevent 'technical leveling' and unfair disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussions with the MEO can inadvertently reveal proprietary information or otherwise 'technically' level the playing field in favor of the MEO, increasing protest risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor comments to the MEO appropriately, avoid revealing contractor proprietary information, and manage communications so they do not advantage one competitor. Maintain documented communication procedures during solicitation and discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) accuracy and scope fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: The PWS is the most important task in an A-76 study; it must accurately reflect the scope and amount of work currently performed and avoid adding work ('gold plating').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to construct an adequate PWS leads to unhappy customers, contract modifications, price escalation, and lost savings. Avoid inflating work (which invites protests). Contracting officers should act as trusted advisors in PWS development, remain involved from the start, and ensure the PWS reflects current operations rather than desired added tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: PWS development methods: work breakdown structure and Activity Based Costing (ABC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use adapted systems-acquisition techniques such as a modified work breakdown structure and Activity Based Costing to develop and validate the PWS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lay out major sub-components of the commercial activity, break them down to an appropriate level, then rebuild and validate requirements up to major components. Adopt ABC to aid validation; if ABC not widely adopted, ensure technical experts familiar with current government operations review the PWS frequently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of the PWS by technical experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification of the PWS requires technical experts familiar with current Government operations reviewing and validating the requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure frequent interaction between technical experts and the activities studied; use ABC and expert review to validate the PWS and avoid deficiencies that lead to post-award modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk identification and comprehensive risk management
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and manage risks across the A-76 lifecycle—study development, solicitation, award, and post-award—rather than focusing narrowly on employee reaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common risks include employee morale/reactive behavior, PWS deficiencies/gold plating, improper communications, source selection deviations from solicitation criteria, improper cost comparisons, contract bundling impacts, and unauthorized changes post-award. Commands often fail to comprehensively identify and mitigate these risks; adopt systematic risk-management processes and document mitigation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding 'gold plating' requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Over-specifying or 'gold plating' requirements in the PWS poses significant risk, inviting protests and undermining competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep requirements to the current level of work performed; resist adding work for command benefit. Use validated work breakdowns and ABC to guard against unnecessary inflation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract bundling/omnibus contract risk and small-business/JWOD/FPI compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Bundling or omnibus contracts may exclude small/disadvantaged firms and mandatory sources (JWOD, Federal Prison Industries); contracting officers must balance economies of scale with statutory small-business and mandatory-source policies (FAR 19.201, JWOD, FAR 8.704).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether bundling will preclude participation by small or mandatory-source vendors. Consider issuing draft solicitations for industry comment to determine willingness of JWOD/FPI/others to participate, and explore subcontracting strategies (primary plus diversified subcontractors) to include small/disadvantaged firms while achieving economies of scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation-phase controls: mirror source-selection procedures to solicitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Source selection procedures must mirror the evaluation standards set forth in the solicitation; improper communications and deviations create protest risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage solicitation-phase risks like other procurements: document communications, adhere to stated evaluation criteria, and avoid improper or unequal exchanges with offerors and the MEO. Tailor MEO communications to avoid technical leveling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award-phase cost-comparison rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: An improper cost comparison in the award phase is a critical risk and can result in reversed awards and appeals (example: Aberdeen Proving Grounds reversal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to the cost-comparison steps outlined in OMB Circular A-76. Validate cost estimates carefully; recognize the potential consequences (appeals, contract reversal, compensation claims) of faulty cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award scope control and prevention of unauthorized direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-award, there is elevated risk of unauthorized changes to the contract and non-authorized personnel directing contractor employees to perform out-of-scope work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with Contracting Officer's Technical Representatives (COTRs) and commands to instruct personnel about appropriate interaction with contractors. Clearly state that only the contracting officer is authorized to change contract scope; train Marines and installation staff accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest-risk management by strict adherence to solicitation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk of protests is managed by following solicitation procedures and using the evaluation criteria as stated; deviations invite protests or overturning of awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use evaluation criteria specified in the solicitation during source selection, document evaluation decisions, and avoid ad hoc deviations. Comptroller General decisions illustrate that following stated procedures minimizes protest risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized best-practices and lessons-learned database
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no centralized database for best practices and lessons learned from completed A-76 studies; DoD should establish and maintain one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: DoD should create an Internet-accessible database within the Acquisition Web (Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Technology), require Services to submit study-end inputs, and focus content on study management, contracting issues, lessons learned, and best practices for PWS development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify OMB Circular A-76 to capture Government cost and past-performance data and enable best-value awards
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB A-76 should be modified to reflect acquisition reform: capture cost and past-performance data on Government activities and allow incorporation of past performance and other non-price factors into evaluation and awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes should permit capturing data similar to what is gathered on commercial firms, include past-performance data in evaluation criteria, and give contracting officers latitude to award on best overall value (technical approaches, management plans) rather than price alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish waiver procedures to protect mission-critical activities
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD should establish waiver procedures installation commanders can use to protect commercial activities deemed mission critical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to create formal waiver mechanisms that installation commanders can use to exempt or protect activities from competitive sourcing where mission-critical considerations warrant it.
